script: I was caught in a warehouse nightmare—my boss tried to destroy my life.. I work at a large warehouse‑style store, in the curbside pickup zone. Customers order on the app, pick a window, we load it into their car. It's a mad‑fast, high‑stress gig. We aim for five minutes, but when 10+ people show up at once and we've got only two of us, wait times can hit 30 minutes. We're annoyed, we hate making people wait, but we do what we can. Most people stay chill after a quick "sorry for the wait, thanks for your patience," but not everyone. So I just finished my 30‑minute break, walked back through the store, and stepped into the curbside area. In the middle of the lot, this huge, pissed‑off dude was standing like a statue. Normally you can only get in through the corner I entered from—taped off with employees—and the exit door that auto‑locks with an RFID tag. He'd followed an employee to the door, grabbed it before it shut, slipped in the back, and was now holding the whole team hostage. He was yelling, "give me my bag NOW, I am going to fuckin' beat all you all ass!" There were about seven of us in that area, and one coworker had taken the lead, trying to calm him down. He was saying things like, "I am sorry for your wait, sir. We have a procedure. We're doing our best. It's crazy busy. You need to go back outside. You can't be in here. Please just leave." Of course, he was not having that. He kept demanding we hand over the bag immediately or he'd attack us. No leads or supervisors jumped in. No security. So the coworker switched tactics. He asked for the man's name, said we'd prioritize his order, but he had to leave. Turns out, the guy was literally the next person in line for his order, and his tantrum had added about five minutes to everyone's wait, including his own. The coworker told him, "sir, your order is next up right here. Just go to your car and we've got it." We got him out the door most of the way. He jammed his hand in the opening to keep it from locking, so he could stay right there while we were moving in and out, still threatening violence. Another coworker fetched his order and walked it over. We had no higher‑up help, no security. What else could we do? The guy ripped the bag out of his hands, said some curse words, and left. His "big important order" was just one pound of generic ground beef from the bulk store. That was why he was threatening to beat and kill minimum‑wage workers over it. Police were called, a manager took statements three hours later. I don't know what action was taken, but customers need a paid membership to shop here, so I hope that membership got revoked. They've revoked them for less.
